question: Does the 1762 sheet's frontier apply to 1756-08-01?
finding: The Spanish-Portuguese de jure frontier did not change between 1756 and 1762. The line had been settled since the Treaty of Alcanices in 1297; the three places where it was disputed or later moved - Olivenza (to Spain in 1801), the Couto Misto (partitioned in 1864) and the Pyrenean exclave of Llivia - are each withheld by name in this production.
war_risk: The Spanish invasion of Portugal ran May to November 1762, so a Paris sheet of 1762 could in principle show a campaign line. This sheet does not: it is titled a geographic map 'dressee d'apres les Cartes du Pays', carries no order of battle, no siege plans and no dated military annotation, and its provincial washes are the civil comarcas.
note: Recorded so a later stage does not have to rediscover it. Since no geometry from this sheet enters production here, the continuity argument is not relied on by anything.
